title: NY Fed: Consumer Confidence Hits Lowest Since 2013
discussion_signal: The post highlights the 44.9% probability of finding a job after job loss, worsening credit-access perceptions, and weaker current and future financial assessments. It interprets the pattern as a low-hire, low-fire environment in which people may pull back because financial security feels fragile rather than because prices alone are rising. This is a public interpretation of the NY Fed measures, not a causal test.
linked_research_question: Does weaker job-finding confidence change consumer behavior even when people do not expect to lose their current jobs, and is the effect different by income and credit access?
limits: The post does not provide a causal estimate of spending or credit behavior
The low-hire/low-fire framing is an interpretation and may not describe every subgroup
Subjective job-finding probabilities are not realized re-employment rates
